\section{Gaussian Space --- Indicator Smoothing}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.IndicatorSmoothing
\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Indicator Smoothing: Introduction}
Conditional Gaussian averaging of indicators preserves their means and approximates them in integral absolute difference. Coupling the averaging noises also shows that averaging contracts rotation variation.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Indicator Smoothing: Results}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian conditional indicator average]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p010-b007}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. The averaged indicator is the function $u_\theta:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$; for a nonintegrable integrand the integral is assigned zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Averaged indicator as Gaussian measure]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_eq_real_measure}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and
$x\in\mathbb R^n$. Then
\[
u_\theta(x)=\gamma_n\bigl(\{y\in\mathbb R^n:\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y\in A\}\bigr),
\]
where $u_\theta(x)=\int 1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$ and $\gamma_n$
is standard Gaussian measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Measurability of membership disagreement]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurableSet_indicatorDisagreement}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ and $\Xi$ be measurable spaces, let $A\subseteq\Xi$ be measurable, and let
$f,g:\Omega\to\Xi$ be measurable maps. Then the set of $z\in\Omega$ for which exactly
one of $f(z)$ and $g(z)$ belongs to $A$ is measurable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Indicator approximation and rotation sensitivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_abs_averagedGaussianIndicator_sub_indicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_eq_real_measure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurableSet_indicatorDisagreement, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let
$\theta\in\mathbb R$. Write $u_\theta(x)=\int
1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$, where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian
measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Then
\[\int\left|u_\theta(x)-1_A(x)\right|\,d\gamma_n(x)=\Pr\!\left(1_A(X)\ne 1_A(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y)\right),\]
where $X,Y$ are independent standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Range of the averaged Gaussian indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_mem_unitInterval}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_eq_real_measure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and
$x\in\mathbb R^n$. For $u_\theta(x)=\int
1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$, where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian
measure, one has $0\le u_\theta(x)\le1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Convergence of averaged Gaussian indicators]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_abs_averagedGaussianIndicator_sub_indicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_abs_averagedGaussianIndicator_sub_indicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_tendsto_zero, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\ge0$ and let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable. If $u_\theta(x)=\int
1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$, then $\int
|u_\theta(x)-1_A(x)|\,d\gamma_n(x)\to0$ as the real parameter $\theta$ tends to $0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Measurability of the Gaussian indicator average]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurable_averagedGaussianIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let
$\theta\in\mathbb R$. The function $x\mapsto\int
1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$ is measurable, where $\gamma_n$ is the
standard Gaussian product measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of averaged Gaussian indicators]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_averagedGaussianIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_mem_unitInterval, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurable_averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, every measurable set $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, and every
real number $\theta$, the function $x\mapsto\int
1_A(\cos(\theta)x+\sin(\theta)y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$ is integrable with respect to standard
Gaussian measure $\gamma_n$ on $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian mean preservation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_averagedGaussianIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_eq_real_measure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianRotation, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\theta\in\mathbb R$.
For $x\in\mathbb R^n$, define
\[
u_\theta(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y),
\]
where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure. Then
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_\theta(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)=\gamma_n(A).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exchange of middle product coordinates]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_middleTranspose}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $E$ be a measurable space and let $\mu$ be an s-finite measure on $E$. The map
$((a,b),(c,d))\mapsto((a,c),(b,d))$ preserves the measure
$(\mu\otimes\mu)\otimes(\mu\otimes\mu)$ on $(E\times E)\times(E\times E)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Independent paired Gaussian mixtures]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianPairedEndpoint}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianRotation, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_middleTranspose, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and $u\in\mathbb R$. If $X_1,X_2,Y_1,Y_2$ are independent
standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb R^n$, then $(\cos u\,X_1+\sin u\,Y_1,\cos
u\,X_2+\sin u\,Y_2)$ has the product of two standard Gaussian laws on $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Difference of finite set measures]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_measureReal_sub_le_symmDiff}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on a measurable space $E$, and let $C,D\subseteq E$. Then
$|\mu(C)-\mu(D)|\le\mu(C\mathbin{\triangle}D)$, where $C\mathbin{\triangle}D$ is their
symmetric difference and the measures are viewed as real numbers.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Coupled bound for averaged indicators]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_pair_diff_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_measureReal_sub_le_symmDiff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_eq_real_measure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianRotation, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and take $u,v\in\mathbb R$ and
$x,x'\in\mathbb R^n$. If $Y,Y'$ are independent standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb
R^n$, then
\[
|u_u(x)-u_u(\cos v\,x+\sin v\,x')|
\le \Pr\!\left(1_A(\cos u\,x+\sin u\,Y)\ne 1_A\bigl(\cos u(\cos v\,x+\sin v\,x')+\sin
u(\cos v\,Y+\sin v\,Y')\bigr)\right),
\]
where $u_u(w)=\int 1_A(\cos u\,w+\sin u\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Averaging contracts rotation variation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_rotation_variation_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_pair_diff_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurableSet_indicatorDisagreement, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianPairedEndpoint, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $u,v\in\mathbb R$. For
independent standard Gaussian vectors $G,G'\in\mathbb R^n$, define $u_u(x)=\int 1_A(\cos
u\,x+\sin u\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$ and let $R_A(v)=\Pr(1_A(G)\ne1_A(\cos v\,G+\sin v\,G'))$.
Then
\[
\mathbb E\left[|u_u(G)-u_u(\cos v\,G+\sin v\,G')|\right]\le R_A(v).
\]
\end{lemma}
